name: PolyDEX PLX Locker (vMToken) claimUnlocked ERC777 reentrancy
summary: vMToken.claimUnlocked (the fPLX token locker) transfers the claimable PLX before increasing _released. PLX is an ERC777-style token that calls the recipient's tokensReceived hook, so an attacker contract re-entered unlockAll()/claimUnlocked 40 times per transaction and was paid the same vested amount repeatedly. Eleven transactions with growing lock sizes drained 59.6M net PLX from the locker, which the attacker sold for USDC and WETH.
notes: The UChildERC20Proxy constructor stored vMToken implementation 0xac8c06c3b3032af783508fad9107d3165ef3fcb8 in the matic.network.proxy.implementation slot (no ProxyUpdated event); the slot and implementation runtime are unchanged until after the exploit (first ProxyUpdated at block 16281056).

Net PLX depletion of the locker across the eleven reentrant transactions (88,158,559.597 out minus 28,525,877.115 locked in by the attacker contracts). Valued by the attacker's disposal: 25 sales of 59,534,251.04 PLX between blocks 15952778 and 15953416 returned 127,336.874416 USDC.e plus 119.239910666 WETH, swapped for 266,831.663730 USDC.e; total 394,168.538146 USD. The disposal crashed the PLX price, so this is a lower bound; PolyDEX reported about 500,000 USD.
